name: Step-up
pattern: Single-leg climb: one foot on a box drives the body up to standing, then lowers under control.
setup: Box about knee height or lower, so your thigh is level or less on the box.
Place your whole working foot on the box, heel included.
Stand tall, weights at your sides or bar on your back.

steps.text: Lean slightly forward over the front foot, weight on its heel.
Push through the box foot to stand up; the back foot just follows.
Stand tall on the box, hip and knee straight, the other foot beside it or knee raised.
Lower the free foot back to the floor slowly, controlled by the box leg.

cues.cue: Lift yourself with the top leg, not a bounce off the floor.
cues.why: Pushing off the back foot takes most of the work away from the box leg.

cues.cue: Box knee in line with your middle toes.
cues.why: The knee drifting inward is a common single-leg fault linked to weak side-hip muscles.

cues.cue: Lean your chest a little over the box foot.
cues.why: A slight forward lean brings the hips into the lift; all step-up versions train the glutes and hamstrings well.

cues.cue: Whole foot on the box, push through the heel.
cues.why: Toes only shift the load to the knee and calf and costs balance.
The lowering half trains control of the knee and hip.

breathing: Breathe out as you step up, in as you lower.

tempo.note: Step up in about 1 second, lower in 2.

mistakes.name: Push off the back foot
mistakes.looks: The floor foot springs up on its toes and does the lifting.
mistakes.fix: Lift your back toes up before you drive, or lower the box.
mistakes.why: The trailing leg steals the work from the box leg.

mistakes.name: Box knee caves in
mistakes.looks: The working knee drifts inward as you stand up.
mistakes.fix: Push the knee out over your little toes; use a lower box.
mistakes.why: Weak hip abductors let the thigh roll in under load.

mistakes.name: Heel hangs off or lifts
mistakes.looks: Only the front of the foot is on the box; the heel rises as you drive.
mistakes.fix: Put the whole foot on the box and drive through the heel.
mistakes.why: Load goes to the knee and calf, and balance suffers.

safety: Use a stable box that cannot slide or tip.
Knee pain: lower the box so the knee bends less than 90° at the start.
Balance: start with bodyweight and hold a rail.

variants.change: Higher box: more hip bend at the start and more glutes.
Box beside you: step up sideways, more side-hip work.
Cross the far leg over to the box.
Lean further forward and drive through the heel for more glutes.
At the top drive the free knee up or step back into a lunge.
Bar on the back or front rack: watch balance and box height.
Arm movement added at the top; keep the stance leg still.

subtypes.name: Lateral step-up
subtypes.change: Stand beside the box and step up sideways; the free leg stays out to the side.

subtypes.name: Step-down (Peterson, Poliquin, Patrick)
subtypes.change: Stand on the box and slowly tap the other heel to the floor in front or to the side, then stand up; knee travels far forward (heel raised in the Peterson and Poliquin versions).

metrics.label: Box knee bend at the start
Box knee inside the foot line (front view)
Push from the floor foot (ankle point, degrees)

motion.basis: Right leg on the box, left leg on the floor. Box knee and hip angles set for a box at about knee height (estimate); muscle emphasis from simenz2012 and muyor2020. Other angles estimated from the movement.

sources.cite: Simenz CJ, Garceau LR, Lutsch BN, Suchomel TJ, Ebben WP. Electromyographical analysis of lower extremity muscle activation during variations of the loaded step-up exercise. J Strength Cond Res. 2012;26(12):3398-3405.

Muyor JM et al. Electromyographic activity in the gluteus medius, gluteus maximus, biceps femoris, vastus lateralis, vastus medialis and rectus femoris during the monopodal squat, forward lunge and lateral step-up exercises. PLoS One. 2020;15(4):e0230841.
Crossley KM, Zhang WJ, Schache AG, Bryant A, Cowan SM. Performance on the single-leg squat task indicates hip abductor muscle function. Am J Sports Med. 2011;39(4):866-873.
